title: Wickens wins the wet Moscow opener and takes the championship lead
dek: Robert Wickens won the rain-hit 22-lap race for Mercedes-AMG from second on the grid, 10.955s ahead of Paul di Resta, in a Mercedes one-two-three-four that moved him top of the standings.

chapters.title: Back from the summer break with a tight table
text: The DTM returned from its summer break at Moscow Raceway, the sixth of the season's nine race weekends, with a 40-minute race on Saturday 20 August and a longer one to follow on Sunday. Zandvoort in July had shared out the wins, Robert Wickens taking Race 1 and Jamie Green Race 2, and it left Marco Wittmann at the head of the table on 105 points. Green was seven behind on 98, Edoardo Mortara third on 88, Wickens fourth on 83 and Paul di Resta fifth on 74, so a win could put Wickens back in contention for the lead.

The first ten races of the year had produced nine different winners, with Mortara the only driver to win twice. Audi had taken five of them, Mercedes three and BMW two. The grid was split evenly between the three makes, eight Audi RS 5, eight BMW M4 and eight Mercedes-AMG C 63 cars, and one of the Mercedes had a new driver. Felix Rosenqvist made his DTM debut in the ART-run #88, taking over from Esteban Ocon.
The weather was the other unknown. Qualifying was held on a damp, drying track, heavy rain returned before the race, and the opening laps would be run behind the safety car.

chapters.title: Mercedes locks out the first two rows
text: Mercedes took the first four places on the grid. Gary Paffett's ART car was fastest on 1:41.443, with Wickens 0.605s behind in the first of the HWA cars, di Resta third at 0.687s and Maximilian Götz fourth at 0.721s. Paffett said the hardest part of the session had been choosing between slicks and wet tyres, and that he had felt the track was still too wet for slicks.

Mattias Ekström was the best of the Audi drivers in fifth, 1.007s off the pole time, and Maxime Martin the best BMW in sixth, 1.063s down. Timo Scheider was seventh, with Timo Glock eighth on exactly the same time of 1:42.631. Rosenqvist, in his first DTM qualifying, was ninth, and Green completed the top ten.

The championship picture was less kind to the men chasing the lead. Wittmann was 20th, 2.413s slower than Paffett, while his closest pursuers fared little better: Green started tenth and Mortara twelfth. Tom Blomqvist was 21st, Daniel Juncadella 22nd, Mike Rockenfeller 23rd and Christian Vietoris last of the 24 cars, 3.357s off the pole time.

chapters.title: Wickens passes Paffett once the safety car peels in
text: Standing water meant the race began behind the safety car, and the field circulated in formation before racing was allowed to start. Paffett led the Mercedes line-up, but Wickens was alongside him almost as soon as the cars were released and took the lead within the first racing laps. Di Resta also got by the pole-sitter, so that three Mercedes headed the race.

Wickens said he had been able to see very little behind the safety car, but that once he was past Paffett the car had a lot of grip and was extremely quick. Paffett said he had not wanted to take undue risks in such conditions. Götz held fourth and kept the other makes behind the Mercedes trio, with Ekström the first Audi and Martin the first BMW.

chapters.title: Rosenqvist scores on his debut as BMW struggles for grip
text: The order behind the leaders was reshuffled by grip rather than by pace. Rosenqvist fought with Glock and Mortara in the early stages, and Mortara got past the Swede, after which Green also came up behind him. Green then passed Mortara as well, so that Audi's two title contenders finished seventh and eighth, ahead of Scheider in ninth. Rosenqvist held on to tenth and took a point on his first DTM start.

Glock slipped from eighth on the grid to 11th and out of the points after struggling for grip in the opening laps, and the BMW drivers generally found the conditions hard going. Juncadella started 22nd and finished last of the 24 cars, but set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:48.220 on lap 21.

chapters.title: Mercedes takes the first four places
text: Wickens completed the 22 laps in 42:29.196 and won by 10.955s from di Resta, with Paffett a further 1.338s behind in third. Götz was fourth, 25.270s behind the winner. Mercedes had therefore filled the first four places just as it had filled the first two rows of the grid, and Wickens collected his second win of the season and the fifth of his DTM career.

Ekström was fifth for Audi, 1.369s ahead of Martin, who scored the only points of the day for BMW with sixth. Green, Mortara, Scheider and Rosenqvist completed the top ten. Wittmann could do nothing to improve on his starting position and finished 19th, 50.288s behind the winner, which left him without points.

The championship swung accordingly. Wickens went to 108 points, three ahead of Wittmann on 105, with Green on 104 and Mortara and di Resta level on 92, so that five drivers were now within 16 points of each other at the top.

facts.v: Wickens, di Resta, Paffett and Götz finished in the first four places, with Paffett dropping from pole position to third.
Heavy rain left so much water on the track that the race began behind the safety car, with Paffett on pole.
